issues.description: Class name identifier mismatch: the UML diagram in problem_statement.md declares a class named 'Course' with the lecture attributes and methods, while both the template and solution repositories define a public class named 'Lecture' in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java. This inconsistency can confuse students about which class name to follow (the UML or the provided Java files) and whether they must rename files or change the UML when implementing the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class name consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: update the UML in problem_statement.md (lines 63-74) to declare the class as 'Lecture' (keeping the listed attributes and methods unchanged) so it matches the template and solution. Alternate fix: rename the Java class and files in the template and solution from 'Lecture' to 'Course' and update any references accordingly.

issues.description: The UML diagram in the problem statement declares the class as 'Course' (identifier: Course) while the exercise text, the template implementation and the solution implementation consistently refer to the same conceptual entity as 'Lecture' (identifier: Lecture). Specifically, problem_statement.md contains the line 'class Course {' which names the entity Course, but template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java declares 'public class Lecture {' and solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java also declares 'public class Lecture {'. This naming mismatch between the UML ('Course') and the Java artifacts ('Lecture') can confuse students about which class they are expected to implement and map between the UML and the provided code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class name consistent across artifacts. Rename the UML class declaration in problem_statement.md from 'Course' to 'Lecture' so the UML matches the template and solution Java classes. Alternatively, if the intended name is 'Course', rename the Java class files and all textual references to 'Course' and update the constructor/usage examples accordingly. Ensure the name used in the UML, the textual instructions, and the template/solution code are identical.
